_comment: Core 5e numbers. Skill and ability names follow the SRD 5.1 (CC-BY-4.0, Wizards of the Coast).

acrobatics.name: Acrobatics
acrobatics.text: Keeping your feet: landing a leap on rough ground, wriggling out of a grapple or a web, running from the watch.

animal_handling.name: Animal Handling
animal_handling.text: Handling beasts: calming an animal that attacks you so that it backs off, and talk of beasts and their keeping.

arcana.name: Arcana
arcana.text: The lore of magic: telling what a magic item does, copying spell scrolls into a spellbook, knowing spells and magical things.

athletics.name: Athletics
athletics.text: Strength in action: climbing, swimming, shoving and grappling, breaking free, forcing a way, running from the watch.

deception.name: Deception
deception.text: Lying well: bluffing in conversation, haggling with a story, passing a disguise or a false tale past the watch.

history.name: History
history.text: Knowing the past: the realms, wars, heroes and old names of this world; old books; knowing people and giants.

insight.name: Insight
insight.text: Reading people: seeing a lie or a hidden motive in conversation, spotting a cheat at cards, sensing a secret society.

intimidation.name: Intimidation
intimidation.text: Frightening people: threats in conversation, making beaten foes give up in a fight, leaning on the guilty.

investigation.name: Investigation
investigation.text: Searching with your head: finding secret doors, traps and hidden things underground, working out clues.

medicine.name: Medicine
medicine.text: Tending the hurt: stopping bleeding, treating wounds, infection and sickness, steadying the dying in a fight.

nature.name: Nature
nature.text: Wild lore: plants, herbs and beasts; herbal remedies for wounds; knowing beasts, dragons, oozes and plants.

perception.name: Perception
perception.text: Noticing things: an ambush or a hidden foe before they strike, traps and secrets underground. The skill used most.

performance.name: Performance
performance.text: Entertaining: playing for coin at inns, music in the evenings, a song or a story in conversation.

persuasion.name: Persuasion
persuasion.text: Winning people round honestly: in conversation, haggling, asking for work or mercy, getting foes to yield.

religion.name: Religion
religion.text: The lore of faiths: gods, rites, temples and cults; knowing undead, fiends and celestials; a cleric's scrolls.

sleight_of_hand.name: Sleight of Hand
sleight_of_hand.text: Deft fingers: picking locks underground (best with thieves' tools), picking pockets, working a cell's lock loose.

stealth.name: Stealth
stealth.text: Moving unseen: slipping past or creeping up on trouble on the road, surprising foes, hiding in a fight.

survival.name: Survival
survival.text: Living off the land: hunting, fishing and foraging at camp, finding the way and water, tracking.

_discovery_xp: Experience for each character, times their level, the first time they enter a region, reach a site (a ruin, a lair, a barrow...) or reach a level under the ground.
_language_lists: Languages (2024 Player's Handbook): everyone speaks Common and two standard languages of their choice; the rare ones come with features. The realm's own tongues (Old Imperial, the Northern Tongue, Southron Cant) count as standard here.
_encounters: Combat encounters by the DMG 2024 (PDF pages 118-119): budget is the XP Budget per Character, [Low, Moderate, High] for levels 1 to 20. A band met in the land is built for the land, not the party (DESIGN.md: some fights should be avoided): danger_level is the party level a region's danger (0-10) stands for; odds how often a band is built Low, Moderate or High; the budget is per character in the party; a band never loses the last of any kind in it, and grows at most to most_extra times its largest roll; tiers (Demigods & Magics, the PHB's tiers of play): where the budget is at least a level's Low per character, a band may grow to that many times its roll (the deep places of the worst lands send hosts against heroes of legend). Danger 0-7 stays as it was: a level 15 party walks through farmland in peace. How a band looks to the player: below Low, Low, Moderate, High, and deadly above deadly times High.

encounters._deeper_level: The party level a dungeon's deeper levels stand for when they reach past danger 7 under an ordinary land (danger 7 or less): one, two, three steps past it.
encounters._legend_hp: A named beast of the history, a barrow king or a dragon at the bottom of a site has grown with its legend: its hit points times this (from the third tier: the game before twenty levels is untouched), by the tier of play of the party's leader when the level is first entered (levels 1-4, 5-10, 11-16, 17-20).

_travel_pace: Travel pace (PHB 2024 PDF page 23, DMG PDF pages 42-43): time for the same ground (4, 3 or 2 miles an hour), and what it does to noticing (a passive score, -5 or +5) and to Survival (finding the way) and Stealth (slipping away); the land's maximum pace (DMG Travel Terrain, by biome or family), one step faster on a good road; where the book says Slow (mountains, marsh) the game's own steps are slow already, so there it only forbids Fast.
_attitudes: Attitudes (PHB 2024 Rules Glossary, DMG PDF pages 36 and 55): Friendly gives advantage on checks to influence them, Hostile disadvantage. A band met on the road starts with an attitude rolled by its leader's alignment (its stat block's), weighted towards Hostile (they are met as trouble); an Indifferent or Friendly band can be let be. A band that has been bloodied in a fight is no longer simply Hostile (Indifferent). Townsfolk's attitude is their mood: hostile or unfriendly people are Hostile, warm or friendly ones Friendly.
_study: The Study action (2024, PHB PDF page 378): the skill by kind of creature (anything else: Arcana), and the DC: base + per_cr x Challenge Rating, at most max (the PHB's scale: easy 10, medium 15, hard 20, very hard 25).
_hazards: The 2024 Rules Glossary's hazards and objects (PHB PDF pages 365, 370, 379), read by rules/engine/hazards.py.
_spell_scrolls: Spell scrolls (DMG 2024 p. 309, by spell level 0-9): the save DC and attack bonus the scroll casts with, its rarity, and its value in copper (twice the PHB 2024 p. 236 cost of scribing it, as the DMG values a scroll).

objects._terrain: What can be broken on a battlefield: terrain id -> [substance, size, resilient, what it becomes ('ground': the field's own ground)].
